pins.name: D3
pins.label: GPIO0 (Button)
pins.notes:
Must be HIGH or floating for normal boot; LOW at boot enters flash/programming mode. No interrupt support. This board's KEY_FLASH pushbutton (vendor datasheet-confirmed, see NOTE above)
KEY_FLASH — onboard user pushbutton (vendor datasheet-confirmed, see NOTE above)

pins.name: D1
pins.label: D1 (GPIO1)
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 TX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: D2
pins.label: D2 (GPIO2)
pins.notes:
Must be HIGH at boot. This board's onboard "L" LED (LED_BUILTIN, vendor datasheet-confirmed) — polarity undocumented, not tagged (see NOTE above)
Onboard "L" LED / LED_BUILTIN (vendor datasheet-confirmed) — polarity undocumented, not tagged led_high/led_low (see NOTE above)

pins.name: D0
pins.label: D0 (GPIO3)
pins.notes: Hardware UART0 RX0 — used by the Serial pfod connection, not available as a general GPIO

pins.name: D10
pins.label: D10 (GPIO15)
pins.notes: Must be LOW at boot (tied to GND via resistor on most boards)

pins.name: D6
pins.label: D6 (GPIO16)
pins.notes: RTC-domain pin: no internal pull-up/down, no PWM, no interrupt support. Commonly wired to RST for deep-sleep wake

pins.name: A0
pins.label: A0 (GPIO17)
pins.notes: Analog input only (A0) — cannot be used for digital I/O or PWM. Board has a vendor-documented onboard resistor divider extending the native 0-1.0V range to 0-3.3V — see adc.defaultRefVolts and NOTE above
